startup.name: truthsystems
startup.one_liner: Automatically blocking risky behavior with real-time governance agents
startup.description: A compliance agent that turns company policies into real-time guardrails on employee use of generative AI, blocking non-compliant actions and matching tool access to user competency. Team of 6 in San Francisco, YC Summer 2025.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting rate of about 1 percent from references/yc_acceptance.md. Up for a timely enterprise problem (shadow AI use was reported by 69 percent of surveyed security leaders) and AI security being a YC interest; down for a crowded field and no stated customers or security founder pedigree. Already listed in Summer 2025, so the ladder is the "if accepted" view.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say the pitch is generic: AI governance and guardrails are already offered by funded startups and by large security vendors, and the description names no customers or proof that policy translation into real time guardrails works better than rules based data loss prevention.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B --calibration-only: seed 59% known only, 65% upper (n=126). Time to seed p25/median/p75 = 3/7/15 months from batch start (n=74).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 16.3 months, 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-17. About 75 percent of eventual seeds land inside that window, so the ever anchor gives about 0.44, and I add under 1.25 times for an AI security category where the closest analogs (Unbound $4M, Credal $4.8M, Dynamo AI $4.15M) all raised institutional seeds. This number does not rank the company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under $3M from angels, a seed fund or a strategic. Most common when the product has early users but no paid base.
Institutional seed in the middle of the 2022 and later table, led by a seed fund after a few months of visible traction.
Larger institutional seed, usually needing paying customers or a standout team story and a competitive process.
Upside seed from a top tier fund in a hot category; rare and needs clear momentum.

ladder.why_it_fails: Enterprise AI governance sells to security and compliance teams with long cycles, and a six person team without named customers will struggle to show revenue. Investors were funding the category, but the analogs that raised were led by founders with security product pedigrees (Palo Alto, Imperva), which this description does not claim, so the likely failure is an inconclusive pilot phase and a small round.

bands.rationale: Thin Series A or extended seed style round after slow revenue; sized like the lower quartile of 2022 and later rounds.
Core Series A near the 2022 and later median of $14M with a pre money in the market range of $50M to $65M.

Credal and Unbound pivoted or repositioned within two years, and Galini moved toward consulting, so many analogs did not reach a Series A.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most paths end in a stall or a quick acquisition by a security or cloud vendor, which is how security tooling categories usually consolidate. The company would need to become the standard control layer for enterprise AI use before large suites copy it, and that is a narrow path for six people.

killers.risk: Large security vendors bundle AI governance
killers.evidence: Palo Alto, Microsoft and Zscaler sell AI usage controls and data loss prevention to the same buyer.
killers.mitigation: Move faster on policy translation and win mid market first.

killers.risk: Long enterprise sales cycles and no early revenue
killers.evidence: Security buyers need pilots and reviews; a six person team has few sales people.
killers.mitigation: Sell to compliance heavy mid market firms with short pilots.

killers.risk: Product is not meaningfully better than rule based blocking
killers.evidence: Blocking tools alone are widely seen as insufficient, but monitoring and sanctioned tool lists cover much of the need.

killers.risk: Category pivots away from this form
killers.evidence: Credal and Galini both repositioned within two years.
killers.mitigation: Keep the policy engine reusable across agents.

technical_complexity.rationale: Intercepting AI interactions through browser or network agents and judging policy compliance with a model is buildable by a small team in three months. The hard parts are low false block rates, latency, enterprise integration and deployment inside corporate security stacks.

takeover_risk.rationale: Security vendors can add policy based AI controls to existing agents and already sell to the same buyers. The startup would be absorbed or squeezed unless it owns a distinct workflow such as competency based access.

evidence.claim: A Gartner survey of 302 security leaders found 69 percent suspect or have evidence of staff using prohibited generative AI, and IBM says shadow AI adds about $670,000 per breach.

brand.name: truthsystems
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "truthsystems" --era 2022+: 12 characters, 1 word, invented or proper kind.
weaknesses: Run together lowercase is hard to read
Truth is a crowded word in AI and media
brand.rationale: The word truth signals trust, which fits compliance, but Systems naming is generic and similar to many security companies. Names like Okta or Wiz are more distinctive, though governance buyers rely on references more than names.

narrative.headline: A timely problem in an AI security category where close analogs raised seeds, but an unproven six person team in a bundling prone field.
narrative.general_summary: Truth Systems builds a compliance agent that enforces company policy on employee AI use in real time. The need is measured, with most security leaders suspecting prohibited AI use. Close analogs Unbound, Credal and Dynamo AI raised seeds of $4M to $4.8M, while Galini and others went quiet or repositioned. Large security vendors can bundle similar controls. For the 16.3 month window the seed probability is near the windowed cohort anchor and later rounds are unlikely. The odds do not rank this company.
